title: What is the highest point above sea level on Earth?
description: The video measures every height from the sea level line, so the highest point above it is the one with the greatest positive height. It names the peak and gives its height, and checks that the height starts at the sea and not at the foot of the mountain.
teaching_notes: One idea: a height above sea level is measured from the sea level line, and the highest place has the greatest positive height. Watch for students who measure a mountain from its own foot instead of from sea level.

video_script.why: The child finds the highest point above sea level on Earth and its height, measured from the sea level line.
video_script.substitution: A tall mountain drawn beside a sea level line, with its height measured up from the line.
video_script.anchor: a sea level line at zero with a very tall mountain peak drawn beside it
video_script.payoff_line: The highest point above sea level has the greatest positive height.

final_answer.value: Mount Everest; its height above sea level is 8848 m.
final_answer.spoken: Mount Everest, which is eight thousand eight hundred and forty eight metres above sea level

hold_back: Mount Everest; its height above sea level is 8848 m.
maths_rules: sea level is the zero line, 0 m
a point above sea level has a positive height; the highest point has the greatest positive height
the highest point above sea level on Earth is Mount Everest, 8848 m above sea level (book's answer key)
a height above sea level is measured from the sea level line, not from the foot of the mountain
check: a place above sea level has no minus sign, so the height is +8848 m
